credits_cram.why: States "CRAM is the method of \citet{hoover2026cram}" and "This paper is a small replication-and-comparison study, not a new method."

cites_hoover.why: Uses \citet{hoover2026cram} in the introduction, the related work and the CRAM methodology section.

small_n.why: Says the direct condition used "5 puzzles each" for Opus and Sonnet and 10 for Haiku, and flags that estimates are "very uncertain".

handset_caveat.why: "The hand-set one-weight energy with no training solved 497/500, matching the learned energy (496--497)".

their_numbers.why: Says 99.996% and 42 ms on an H200 are "their number and not measured by us", and that the authors' code was not run.

no_new_claims.why: Adds figures not supported by the log: "9 of the 12 non-solves" (the log gives 11), a ~1% cost ratio (actually ~5-10%), and Wilson intervals and a rule-of-three bound.
